items.prompt: I ___ reading when Mum called me.

options.why: Were goes with you, we and they. With I, we use was.
Called is in the past, so we need a past form.
Has is not used with an -ing verb like this.

hints: Called tells you this is in the past.
The past progressive uses was or were with an -ing verb.
Which one goes with I?
items.explanation: With I in the past, we use was: I was reading. The reading was going on when Mum called.

items.prompt: They ___ playing football at four o'clock yesterday.

options.why: Was goes with I, he, she or it. They needs a different word.
Is is the present tense.
Have does not go with playing here.

hints: Yesterday tells you this is in the past.
They means more than one person.
Was or were: which one goes with they?
items.explanation: With they in the past, we use were: they were playing.

items.prompt:
Use the past progressive of paint.
Dewi ___ when it started to rain.
hints: The painting was already going on when the rain started.
Use was or were, then add -ing to the verb.
Dewi is one person. Which helper word goes with her?
items.explanation: The past progressive uses was or were with an -ing verb: Dewi was painting.

items.prompt: We have ___ our homework.

options.why: After have, we need the past form.
Finishing goes with am, is, are, was or were.
Finishes is the present tense.

hints: Have is a helper verb here.
The present perfect uses has or have with a past form.
Many past forms end in -ed.
items.explanation: The present perfect is has or have with a past form: we have finished.

items.prompt: Leo ___ lost his pencil case.

options.why: Have goes with I, you, we and they.
Is lost would mean something different here.
Were is not used with lost like this.

hints: Leo is one person.
Use has with he, she or it. Use have with I, you, we and they.
Swap Leo for he. Which helper word fits?
items.explanation: Leo is one person, like he, so we use has: Leo has lost his pencil case.

items.prompt: Match each verb to the form used after has or have.
hints: These verbs have a special form after has or have.
Say: I have ... with each one.
Start with see. I have ... that film.
items.explanation: After has or have, these verbs use special past forms: eaten, gone, seen, written and taken.

items.prompt:
Use the right form of ride.
Have you ever ___ a horse?
hints: After have, you need the special past form.
Ride is irregular. It does not add -ed.
Think of write and written. Ride changes in a similar way.
items.explanation: The form of ride after have is ridden: Have you ever ridden a horse?

items.prompt: Sort the phrases into the past progressive and the present perfect.
hints: Look at the helper word in each phrase.
Was and were go with -ing. Has and have go with a past form.
Start with she was singing. Which helper word does it use?
items.explanation: Was or were with an -ing verb is the past progressive. Has or have with a past form is the present perfect.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that one action was interrupted by another?

options.why: This shows only one finished action.

options.text: I was walking home when it started to rain.

options.why: This shows a finished action with nothing interrupting it.
This is about the future.

hints: An interrupted action was still going on when something else happened.
Look for a sentence with two actions.
The longer action uses was or were with -ing.
items.explanation: I was walking home shows an action that was going on. When it started to rain shows what interrupted it.

items.prompt:
Use the verbs watch and go.
We ___ a film when the lights ___ out.
hints: The film was already going on. Then something happened suddenly.
The longer action uses were with -ing. The sudden action uses the simple past.
Do the first gap first: we were ...
items.explanation: We were watching shows that the film was going on. The lights went out is the sudden action that interrupted it.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: She has gone to the shop.
She has went to the shop.
options.why: After has, we use gone, not went.

options.text: She have gone to the shop.
options.why: She needs has, not have.

options.text: She was gone to the shop.
options.why: We do not use was with gone like this.

hints: She needs has.
After has, use the special past form of go.
Is it went or gone after has?
items.explanation: With she we use has, and after has we use gone: she has gone to the shop.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: I have seen that film yesterday.
options.why: We do not use have seen with a finished time like yesterday.

options.text: I have saw that film yesterday.
options.why: After have we use seen, and yesterday needs the simple past.

options.text: I was seen that film yesterday.
options.why: Was seen is not correct here.

hints: Yesterday is a finished time.
The present perfect is not used with a finished time like yesterday.
Which sentence uses the simple past?
items.explanation: Yesterday is a finished time, so we use the simple past: I saw that film yesterday. Without yesterday, we could say I have seen that film.

items.prompt: Last night my sister ___ drawing a map.

options.why: Were is for more than one person. Sister is just one.
Is is for now. Last night is in the past.
Has needs a past form, not -ing.

hints: Is it one person or more?
Last night is in the past.
Choose the past helper for one person.
items.explanation: My sister is one person, and last night is past, so we say was drawing.

items.prompt: Mum has ___ the shopping.

options.why: Has needs a past form, not buy.
Buying needs was or were, not has.
Buy is irregular, so it does not take -ed.

hints: Has needs a past form.
Buy is an irregular verb.
Say: Yesterday I bought.
items.explanation: Has bought uses the past form of buy: bought.

items.prompt: Sekar and I ___ chopping onions while Bayu ___ stirring the soup.
hints: Count the people in each part.
Sekar and I is more than one person.
Bayu is one person.
items.explanation: Sekar and I is more than one, so were. Bayu is one person, so was.

items.prompt:
Use the right form of eat.
Kofi has ___ all his lunch.
hints: Has needs a past form.
Eat is an irregular verb.
It ends in -en.
items.explanation: Has eaten uses the past form of eat: eaten.

items.prompt:
Use has or have.
The twins ___ finished their drawings.
hints: Is the subject one or more than one?
Twins is more than one.
Plural subjects use have.
items.explanation: The twins is plural, so we say have finished.

items.prompt: Match each verb to the form used after has or have.
hints: These verbs are irregular.
The forms after has or have often end in -en.
Start with write. Not wrote.
items.explanation: After has or have we use the past participle: taken, broken, written, driven, chosen.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.why: Wrote is the simple past. After has we say written.
Yuki is one person, so we say has.
Were does not fit with written here.

hints: Is Yuki one person or more?
Check the helper word first.
Then check the verb form.
items.explanation: Yuki is one person, so has. Write becomes written after has.

items.prompt: Build a sentence about walking home in the rain.
items.answer: We were walking home when it began to rain.
hints: It starts with We.
Use were with -ing.
The second part starts with when.
items.explanation: We were walking is the past progressive. It began to rain interrupted it.

items.prompt: Amara went to the beach. She collected shells and builds a sandcastle. Then she swam. Which verb must change to keep the story in the past?

options.why: Went is already past.
Collected is already past.
Swam is already past.

hints: Read the passage in order.
Which verb is not about the past?
Check each verb.
items.explanation: Builds is present. The story is in the past, so it must be built.

items.prompt: Sort the verb forms by when we use them.
hints: Which forms can follow has?
Has ate and has saw sound wrong.
Start with eaten. Has eaten or has ate?
items.explanation: We say has eaten, has seen and has gone, but I ate, I saw and I went.

items.prompt:
Use the verbs play and start.
The children ___ outside when it ___ to rain.
hints: Fill the first gap, then the second.
The first action was in progress.
Use were with -ing, then the simple past.
items.explanation: Were playing was in progress when it started to rain.

items.prompt: Dewi ___ the plants when her little brother picked a flower.

options.why: This does not show the action was in progress.
Has does not fit with when and picked.
Is is for now.

hints: One action was in progress.
The other action interrupted it.
Use was or were with -ing.
items.explanation: Dewi was watering shows the action was in progress when her brother interrupted.

items.prompt: Last Sunday Leo ___ to the lake. While he ___ along the path, he ___ a duck.
hints: The whole story is in the past.
The middle gap needs an action in progress.
The last action interrupted it.
items.explanation: Leo walked to the lake. While he was walking, he saw a duck.

items.prompt: Which sentence tells us Rangga is back home?

options.text: Rangga has been to the market.
Rangga has gone to the market.
options.why: Has gone means he is still away.

options.text: Rangga is going to the market.
options.why: Is going means he is on the way.

options.text: Rangga was going to the market.
options.why: Was going does not say he came back.

hints: Think about where Rangga is now.
Has gone and has been are different.
Which one means he has come back?
items.explanation: Has been means he went and came back. Has gone means he has not come back yet.

items.prompt: Yesterday Citra visited the museum. She was looking at old coins when a guide came over. He has shown her a gold coin. Then they went to the next room. Which sentence has the wrong tense?

options.why: Visited is correct for yesterday.

options.text: She was looking at old coins when a guide came over.
options.why: Was looking and came are correct for a past story.

options.text: He has shown her a gold coin.
Then they went to the next room.
options.why: Went is correct for a past story.

hints: The story is told in the past.
Which sentence uses a different tense?
Look for has or have.
items.explanation: The story is in the simple past. Has shown does not fit, so it should be showed her a gold coin.

items.prompt: Which sentence tells us Mia still lives in Bandung?

options.text: Mia lived in Bandung for five years.
options.why: Lived shows it is finished.

options.text: Mia was living in Bandung last year.
options.why: Last year shows the past.

options.text: Mia lived in Bandung when she was five.
options.why: When she was five shows the past.

options.text: Mia has lived in Bandung for five years.

hints: Which sentence links the past to now?
Look for has or have.
Compare lived with has lived.
items.explanation: Has lived tells us it began in the past and is still true now.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "I was reading when the bell rang" uses the past progressive.
hints: Find the verb phrase was reading.
It uses was plus an -ing verb.
The action was in progress.
items.explanation: The past progressive uses was or were with an -ing verb to show an action in progress in the past: was reading.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "They are playing in the garden" uses the past progressive.
hints: Look at the helping verb.
Is are past or present?
Are shows now.
items.explanation: Are playing is the present progressive. The past progressive needs was or were, as in they were playing.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "She has finished her homework" uses the present perfect.
hints: Find the helping verb.
It is has plus finished.
Has or have signals the present perfect.
items.explanation: The present perfect uses has or have with a past form of the verb. Has finished links the past to now.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "He have eaten his lunch" is correct.
hints: Which helping verb goes with he?
Compare with I have.
He needs has.
items.explanation: With he, she or it we use has, so the correct sentence is He has eaten his lunch.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "We was walking to school" is correct.
hints: Which form of be goes with we?
Was is for one person.
Use were.
items.explanation: With we we use were, so the correct sentence is We were walking to school.

items.prompt: True or false: The present perfect is made with has or have and the past form of a verb.
hints: Think of an example such as I have seen.
Name the helping verbs.
It uses has or have.
items.explanation: Has or have plus a past form gives the present perfect, for example they have gone.

items.prompt: She ___ finished her work.
hints: She is one person.
Use has with she.
Has goes with he, she, it.
items.explanation: With she, we use has: she has finished.

items.prompt: I ___ reading when you called.
hints: I is one person.
Past progressive uses was or were.
Use was with I.
items.explanation: With I we use was: I was reading.
